extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons administrative users (Signing Officials, Account Administrators, Business Officials), PIs, ASSTs, FSRs and other delegates who manage delegations, ESI checks, and FFRs
extracted.subtask_short: eRA Commons delegation and FFR procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step operational guidance for granting, editing, searching, and revoking delegation authorities in the eRA Commons Admin module, checking ESI eligibility, and using the Federal Financial Report (FFR) module (including search and due-date rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search criteria for locating users (delegations)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can enter an exact Commons ID; no wildcards are allowed. Alternatively, in the Name field type a few letters of the last name to get a list of matches; matches will not appear for first names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always enter the last name in the Name field (e.g., for Sarah Johnson enter 'johnson', not 'Sarah'). Matching records display in the Search Results. You may also select one or more roles (Ctrl+click) in some searches to narrow results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step flow for creating third-party delegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegating authority on behalf of another user is a two-step process: first find/select the user who currently holds the authority (delegator), then find/select the user who will receive the authority (delegate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the three-dot ellipsis menu and the Select option for the delegator, then repeat the search to locate and select the delegate; the system shows a message indicating the selected delegator before you choose the delegate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toggle-and-save mechanism to grant or revoke specific authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities (e.g., Progress Report, Sponsor, PPF, xTrain) are turned on or off using toggles on the Edit/Select Delegations or Delegate Authority popups and then saved to apply changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After turning the appropriate toggle(s) on or off, click Save. A success message appears when completed. Turning a toggle off revokes the authority; turning it on bestows it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email notification on change of delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: When delegation is granted, edited, or revoked, the affected delegate receives an email informing them of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The My Current Delegates screen updates to reflect changes (new delegates appear under Current Delegates; revoked delegates are removed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress Report delegation capability and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: When Progress Report authority is delegated, the delegate can initiate and work on progress reports for the delegator PI, but the delegate is not able to route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After enabling the Progress Report toggle and saving, the system bestows Progress Report authority to the chosen delegate and notifies them by email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based constraints on which authorities can be delegated
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all roles can delegate all authorities. The authorities available for delegation depend on both the role of the granting user and the role of the selected delegate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Delegations table (Delegations topic) for role-based constraints. Example: an ASST can be assigned multiple delegations; a PI can only be delegated PPF and Progress Report; a Trainee can only be delegated PPF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can delegate Sponsor authority on behalf of a Sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: SO (Signing Official) and AA (Account Administrator) can delegate Sponsor authority to someone with an ASST role on behalf of a Sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authorizes the ASST to perform xTrain functions for that Sponsor. Not all roles can delegate Sponsor authority—consult the Delegations table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional delegation of Submit Progress Report authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing officials and business officials can delegate Submit Progress Report authority to PIs within their institution to allow them to submit RPPRs and Final RPPRs electronically to NIH; authority can be revoked at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting/revoking Submit authority is done via the Institution Delegations screen (Current Delegates and Candidates for Delegation tabs). Note agency-specific exceptions: delegations cannot be used for Department of Commerce (DOC) awards and SAMHSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the Candidates for Delegation table
rubrics_metrics.description: The Candidates for Delegation tab lists all users in your organization eligible for submit authority; the table supports filtering, column show/hide, download/print, and bulk actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the checkbox(es) in the first column for users you wish to grant; for many users use the bulk action tool to Select All or Deselect All. After selection, click Allow Delegation(s) to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirement to grant institutional submit authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Before delegating Submit Progress Report authority you must review and accept a certification/acceptance agreement certifying statements are true and that you accept obligations to comply with PHS terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Review Allow Delegation(s) screen click I Agree to certify and confirm the delegation. The system returns you to Institution Delegation and displays a success message after confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to revoke institutional Submit Progress Report authority
rubrics_metrics.description: To revoke institutional Submit Progress Report authority, mark the checkboxes for current delegates, click Revoke Delegation(s), review the revoke confirmation, click I Agree, and the delegations are removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bulk action tool for many users. Revoked delegates receive an email informing them of the change and no longer appear in Current Delegates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct delegations (delegating your own account access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Commons users may delegate authority directly to another Commons user so that user can access features of the grant account or personal account (e.g., RPPR, Personal Profile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access via Admin -> Delegations -> Search or Add Delegate. The authorities available vary by the grant-holder's role and the chosen user's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of delegable authorities (direct delegation list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible direct delegations include: Progress Report authority (PI -> any active user in same org), Status authority (PI -> ASST to use Status feature), PPF authority (any active user -> another to edit Personal Profile), xTrain authority (PI -> ASST), and SPONSOR authority (Sponsor -> ASST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The availability of each delegation type depends on the roles involved and agency-specific restrictions (e.g., DOC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using roles to narrow potential delegate search
rubrics_metrics.description: When searching for potential delegates you can select one or more roles (Ctrl+click) from the Roles list to filter results; role selection helps narrow the search because delegation options differ by role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: selecting ASST will surface users able to accept multiple delegations while selecting PI or Trainee limits visible delegation options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Delegation(s) screen behavior and Select All
rubrics_metrics.description: The Select Delegation(s) screen shows the selected user and toggles for the authorities available for delegation; click Select All to toggle all available authorities on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn on desired toggles and click Save. The chosen user receives an email and My Current Delegates shows checkmarks for conferred authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing delegations for your account
rubrics_metrics.description: To edit delegations for your own account, use the My Current Delegates screen, choose Edit Delegations from the three-dot menu for a delegate, toggle authorities on/off and Save.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA Commons sends an email informing the delegate of the change. If all authorities are revoked the user no longer appears in the My Current Delegates table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting all delegations for a user
rubrics_metrics.description: To remove all delegations at once, use Delete Delegations from the three-dot menu and confirm the delete in the popup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, remove specific authorities by turning off individual toggles and clicking Save; the user receives an email and the My Current Delegates table updates accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI (Early Stage Investigator) eligibility definition and access
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI is a PI who completed their terminal research degree or end of post-graduate clinical training within the past 10 years and who has not yet competed successfully for a substantial NIH independent research award. Only SOs and AOs can access the ESI Eligibility screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESI status matters because NIH policies prioritize awards for ESIs. Access ESI via Status module -> ESI Eligibility or Admin -> ESI Eligibility. Search by name using the format 'Last Name, First Name' and export the list to CSV for sorting (the screen list itself is not sortable).

rubrics_metrics.name: FFR (Federal Financial Report) module role requirement (FSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A user must possess the FSR Commons role to view, enter, and submit FFRs in the FFR module; SO or Account Administrator can add this role to a user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A user who only has the FSR role can perform only FFR-related tasks; signing officials or BO/AO can also have the FSR role.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS requirement to use PMS for SF-425 long form
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning January 1, 2021, HHS grant recipients are required to submit the SF-425 long form in the Payment Management System (PMS) instead of using the eRA Commons FFR module; eRA redirects HHS users to PMS for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register with PMS and obtain PMS login credentials before submitting an FFR. Familiarize with PMS documentation and use the PMS Help Desk for issues. See referenced NOT-OD notices for transition details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and features available in the FFR module
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFR module lets FSRs search for awards with associated FFRs, initiate an FFR (redirects to PMS for HHS awardees), view FFR PDFs, and view submission history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS requires all financial expenditure data to be submitted via PMS; Commons help icons ('?') on FFR screens link to detailed help and a PDF user guide is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFR reporting frequency and annual due date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for SNAP awards, multi-year funded awards, and awards requiring more frequent reporting, the FFR is required annually for each budget period and must be submitted no later than 90 days after the end of the calendar quarter in which the budget period ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide maps budget-period-end calendar quarters to FFR due dates (e.g., budget period ending Jan–Mar -> FFR due June 30). If only start or end dates are entered in date-range searches, behavior is inclusive from that date forward or backward respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-annual FFR due date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When an FFR is required semi-annually, it must be submitted no later than 30 days after the end of the reporting period. Reporting periods are October–March and April–September with due dates April 30 and October 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these dates to determine semi-annual due dates unless the award specifies different reporting frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final FFR status rules (Pending / Due / Late)
rubrics_metrics.description: For final FFRs the due date/status is based on Project Period End Date (PPED): 'Pending' if within 90 days before PPED and not submitted; 'Due' if between PPED and 120 days past PPED and not submitted; 'Late' if more than 120 days past PPED and not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor PPED-based windows to determine final FFR status and follow institutional processes to submit on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFR search guidance and recommended specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: When searching for FFRs, enter as many search criteria as possible to narrow results; overly broad searches can return very large record sets and slow response time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dropdowns and quick searches. Click Reset Search to clear and re-run queries. Quick searches include Received, Pending/Due/Late, Due this year.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFR search fields and expected behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fields include Activity (3-character code), IC (required; defaults to All), Serial (grant serial number), Year, Due Date Start/End, Project Number (enter at least 4 characters), Awarding Office/IC selection, and Status (multi-select).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due Date Start/End: if only start is entered records on that date and after are returned; if only end is entered records on that date and before are returned. Status options include Pending, Due, Late, Received, In Review, Accepted, Rejected, Revision Pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFR search results actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results display below search criteria; use the three-dot ellipsis menu on rows to view available actions for each FFR record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After performing a quick search, click the three-dot menu to act on the record; use Reset Search to clear results and show quick searches if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table tools and export capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables in various screens (e.g., Candidates for Delegation, ESI list) support filter, show/hide columns, download/print and export to CSV for offline sorting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the on-screen list is not sortable (e.g., ESI list), export to CSV and open in Excel or similar to sort and manipulate data.
